title: Chapter 5.  Polity & Governance — The Sixth Schedule Framework

blocks.content: Meghalaya is one of the clearest, most complete real-world examples of the Sixth Schedule's Autonomous District Council system in operation — all three of its major tribal areas have their own ADCs, making this chapter essential for understanding the Sixth Schedule generally, not just for Meghalaya-specific exams.

Under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution (Article 244(2)/275(1)) — the same constitutional mechanism referenced as an aspirational demand for Ladakh in the companion Ladakh GS volume — Meghalaya's three traditional hill divisions (Chapter 1) each have their own elected Autonomous District Council (ADC), exercising legislative, judicial and executive powers over specified local subjects including land, forests, village/town administration, inheritance, marriage and divorce, and social customs.

These ADCs continued to function even after Meghalaya's full statehood in 1972 — an important structural point: the Sixth Schedule ADCs operate ALONGSIDE and in addition to the ordinary state government/Assembly structure, rather than being replaced by it, giving Meghalaya a genuinely dual-layered governance system for tribal-customary matters.

★ EXAM POINT: Meghalaya's THREE Sixth Schedule Autonomous District Councils (KHADC, JHADC, GHADC) operate ALONGSIDE the ordinary state Assembly/government — a dual-layer governance structure, and a frequently tested example when Sixth Schedule ADCs are discussed generally in polity questions (contrast with Ladakh, which does NOT currently have Sixth Schedule status, per the companion Ladakh GS volume).

cells: Unicameral — Meghalaya Legislative Assembly, 60 elected seats, with 55 seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes (an exceptionally high proportion, reflecting Meghalaya's overwhelming tribal population majority)
Conrad Sangma (National People's Party, NPP), in office continuously since 6 March 2018 (re-elected/continued after the 2023 Assembly election)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Meghalaya's Assembly has 55 of 60 seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes — one of the highest ST-reservation proportions of any Indian state Assembly, directly reflecting the state's roughly 86% tribal population share (Chapter 7).

items: Sixth Schedule (Art. 244(2)/275(1)) applies fully to Meghalaya via 3 ADCs: KHADC (Shillong), JHADC (Jowai), GHADC (Tura) — operating alongside the state government.
60-seat Assembly: 55 ST-reserved seats (one of India's highest ST-reservation proportions).
Current CM: Conrad Sangma (NPP), continuously in office since 6 March 2018; Deputy CMs Prestone Tynsong and Sniawbhalang Dhar.
Current Governor: C.H. Vijayashankar, since 30 July 2024.
Meghalaya High Court, Shillong; 2 Lok Sabha seats; 1 Rajya Sabha seat.
